why: How a document lock names a session to everyone who can see it. A session id is the credential a request authenticates with, and lock events reach every member of a shared planner, so what travels is a one-way digest the server and every tab derive the same way: the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over a domain prefix and the session id, as lowercase hex. The server builds it in Go and a tab builds its own in JavaScript to recognise itself; a drift between the two leaves a tab unable to tell that it holds the lock.
